stops.note: 'foreign, babbling', a word imitating unintelligible speech
the Romans used the word for peoples beyond their control, including those of North Africa
Arab writers took the name for the peoples of the Maghreb; many Berbers prefer their own name, Amazigh
used by Europeans; the Barbary Coast and 'Barbary' have the same source

current_meaning: a member of the indigenous peoples of North Africa
